text.p: The following is a profile of Mexico, which faces critical mid-term elections on Sunday in which the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) may suffer its biggest upset in 68 years of power.
AREA: 759,529 sq miles (1,967,183 sq km), with a varied geography ranging from lowland swamp to desert.
GEOGRAPHY: Mexico is bounded by the United States to the north, Guatemala to the south and Belize to the southeast. Its border with the United States is 1,864 miles (3,107 km) long.
POPULATION: 91.5 million (1995 estimate), with nearly a fifth -- about 17 million people -- crowded into the Mexico City valley ringed by volcanos and mountains.
Most Mexicans are mestizos, a blend of European and indigenous ancestry, with Indian blood predominating.
LANGUAGE: Spanish is the dominant language, but eight percent of the population also speak an indigenous language.
RELIGION: Ninety percent of Mexicans identify themselves as Catholic.

HISTORY: Mexico, named after the Mexica tribe which inhabited the central highlands when the Spaniards arrived in 1519, fell under Spanish rule two years later after Hernan Cortes defeated the Aztec stronghold of Tenochtitlan.
For the next 300 years, Spain ruled Mexico, which then included much of what is today the U.S. Southwest including Texas and California, and extracted its silver and gold.
After a failed uprising led by Father Miguel Hidalgo in 1810, Mexico won its independence from Spain in 1821.
Out of the turmoil following the 1910-17 Mexican Revolution was born in 1929 the National Revolutionary Party (PNR), which in 1946 became today's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
The PRI still runs the federal government, the presidency and 27 of the country's 31 states after 68 years of uninterrupted rule.
Currency: The peso. Current exchange rate is 7.95 pesos per dollar
